note: What the United States asks of a visitor, by passport, for the fifty states, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands (Guam and the Northern Marianas add their own waiver; American Samoa keeps its own entry law). Nationals of the Visa Waiver Program's 42 countries come for up to 90 days with an ESTA travel authorisation instead of a visa (8 U.S.C. 1187(a)(1); the program's countries as the official ESTA site lists them, read 2026-10-29: Romania, designated in January 2025, isn't among them, its designation having been rescinded in May 2025); for the United Kingdom that is only British citizens, not British overseas territories' citizens, whose territory passports therefore need a visa unless named below. A Gibraltar passport is a British citizen's, and every British citizen has the right of abode in the United Kingdom, so it is the United Kingdom's rule. Canadian citizens and citizens of Bermuda need no visa (8 CFR 212.1(a)(1)-(2); the E, K, S and V categories aside), nor do citizens of the Marshall Islands, Micronesia and Palau, who under their Compacts of Free Association may enter, work and live in the United States. Bahamians need no visa when pre-cleared by US immigration in the Bahamas; British subjects resident in the Cayman Islands or the Turks and Caicos only arriving directly with a court certificate of no criminal record; nationals of the British Virgin Islands resident there only to visit the US Virgin Islands, or flying on from St Thomas with a police certificate: those conditions aren't modelled, so those passports are taken to need none. Every other passport needs a visa (8 CFR 212.1, opening). The days a visitor with a visa or none may stay are set at admission, not by the list.

sources.title: 8 CFR 212.1, Documentary requirements for nonimmigrants (eCFR, current)
sources.said: A valid unexpired visa that meets the requirements of part 215, subpart B, of this chapter, if applicable, and an unexpired passport, shall be presented by each arriving nonimmigrant alien ... ( 1 ) Canadian citizens. A visa is generally not required for Canadian citizens, except those Canadians that fall under nonimmigrant visa categories E, K, S, or V ... ( 2 ) Citizens of the British Overseas Territory of Bermuda. A visa is generally not required for Citizens of the British Overseas Territory of Bermuda ... ( 3 ) Bahamian nationals or British subjects resident in the Bahamas. A passport is required. A visa required of such an alien unless, prior to or at the time of embarkation for the United States on a vessel or aircraft, the alien satisfied the examining U.S. immigration officer at the Bahamas, that he or she is clearly and beyond a doubt entitled to admission ... ( 4 ) British subjects resident in the Cayman Islands or in the Turks and Caicos Islands. A passport is required. A visa is required of such an alien unless he or she arrives directly from the Cayman Islands or the Turks and Caicos Islands and presents a current certificate from the Clerk of Court of the Cayman Islands or the Turks and Caicos Islands indicating no criminal record. ( b ) Nationals of the British Virgin Islands. A visa is not required of a national of the British Virgin Islands who has his or her residence in the British Virgin Islands, if: ( 1 ) The alien is seeking admission solely to visit the Virgin Islands of the United States; or ... ( d ) Citizens of the Freely Associated States, formerly Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands. Citizens of the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the Federated States of Micronesia may enter into, lawfully engage in employment, and establish residence in the United States and its territories and possessions
